segments.translation_text: The Condensed Vehicle states that the cause of not rising above samsara is attachment to position and spouse; the first two perfections are an antidote for that. One may temporarily rise above samsara yet still return due to incorrect practice and reluctance to perform hardship; the two middle perfections are an antidote for that. One may not return, yet one’s efforts may still be wasted due to distraction and ignorance; the last two perfections are an antidote for that. Thus, based on the antidotes to what needs to be abandoned, it is certain that the number of perfections is six.

segments.translation_text: The six motivations are: - Being unsatisfied with giving only the seven precious jewels such as gold, lapis lazuli, crystal, black pearl, and the like with as many emanation bodies as there are grains of sand on the Ganges River to every sentient being every moment for as many eons as there are grains of sand on the Ganges River is insatiability. For the same duration of time, and the same number of bodies as just described, if even the three worlds of existence were to be completely filled with blazing fire, to still preserve the four types of conduct, despite lack of any material possessions and to look forward to practices such as morality and the like is the motivation of insatiable engagement. - To not allow decline for even a single moment, and to continue to practice uninterruptedly until enlightenment is reached is vast motivation. - To have the joy of thinking that sentient beings benefit me outshone by the joy of benefiting sentient beings through the six perfections is the motivation of joy. - Thinking that as the beings who received benefit have become my spiritual friends, they greatly benefited me, yet I did not benefit them very much is the motivation of beneficial thought. - Not having any expectation of reward or result in response from those who received benefit is motivation without defect. - Thus sharing all meritorious deeds with all sentient beings collectively, and completely dedicating them to achieving great enlightenment is virtuous motivation.

The antidote is realization of the selflessness of phenomena, through which one possesses primordial wisdom of the non-conceptualization of the three cycles. The ultimate result is placing sentient beings in the nirvana of one of the three vehicles suitable to their motivation. Thus beings are completely matured through the four dharmas. segments.translation_text: Householder Bodhisattvas should dwell in giving Dharma and giving materials. Renunciates should dwell in giving Dharma and materials such as pens, ink, and scriptures. Those who have reached the stage of patience of unborn phenomena should dwell in the three types of giving which are: giving which is making a gift of one’s kingdom; great giving which is making a gift of one's spouse, son, or daughter; and greatest giving which is making a gift of one’s head, limbs, eyes, skin, marrow, and the like. The ability to give these gifts should be developed gradually. Impure giving should be discarded, such as giving gifts of poison, weapons, slaughtered meat, alcohol, and the like. Dwelling in pure giving brings both temporary and ultimate benefit to the recipients.

segments.translation_text: The good quality of vastness is giving anything that other beings need. The good quality of freedom from materialism is not having expectations of reward and result. The good quality of great purpose is placing those gathered by giving in one of the three types of enlightenment. The good quality of inexhaustibility is continuing without ceasing, even in the state of nirvana without remainder.
